name: MonarchFavoritesList
title: FavoritesList
wrapsNative: Section in a List, ForEach with .onMove(perform:) and .onDelete(perform:), .environment(\.editMode, …) on the section, MonarchButton (ghost) as the Edit button
summary: A sidebar section of pinned destinations with a starred heading, the current destination marked, and an Edit button that turns on reorder and delete for that section.
whenToUse: In a sidebar or navigation list where people pin projects, views or documents and want to reorder or unpin them.
whenNotToUse: For the app's fixed destinations, use a plain List section or a TabView. For reordering arbitrary content, use a List with onMove (see reorderable-list).
api: init(items: [MonarchFavoriteItem], isEditing: Binding<Bool>? = nil, showsIcon: Bool = true, emptyMessage: String? = nil, labels: MonarchFavoritesListLabels = MonarchFavoritesListLabels(), onRemove: (@MainActor (MonarchFavoriteItem) -> Void)? = nil, onReorder: (@MainActor ([MonarchFavoriteItem]) -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchFavoriteItem) -> Void)
struct MonarchFavoriteItem: Identifiable { init(_ title: String, id: String, systemImage: String? = nil, isCurrent: Bool = false) }
struct MonarchFavoritesListLabels { var title, edit, editLabel, done, removed, moveUp, moveDown: String? }

options.name: items
options.description: The pinned destinations, in order. isCurrent marks the screen the person is on.

options.name: isEditing
options.description: Edit mode controlled by the app. Without it the Edit button keeps its own state.

options.name: showsIcon
options.description: Whether a star comes before the heading.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: Shown when there are no items. Without it the section is left out when empty.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Favorites, Edit, Edit favorites, Done, the removal announcement and the move actions.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes an item. With it rows can be deleted, by swipe or in edit mode.

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Receives the new order. With it rows show a reorder handle in edit mode.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Opens a destination when its row is tapped outside edit mode.

states.name: browsing
states.description: Rows are buttons with an optional icon and the name; the Edit button shows when onRemove or onReorder is given.

states.name: current
states.description: The current destination is semibold in the accent's strong text on its subtle fill, with the selected trait.

states.name: editing
states.description: The section's rows show the system delete control and, with onReorder, the reorder handle; rows stop opening their destination; the button reads Done.

states.name: empty
states.description: With emptyMessage, the heading and the message in muted text; without it nothing is drawn.

appearance: A list section whose heading is a star and a label in the muted text role. Rows use the default text role with muted icons; the current row uses the accent's subtle fill and strong text, which keep their contrast in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web FavoritesList is a nav of links with its own remove buttons and a ReorderableList. On iOS the section sits in the app's List and uses the system's edit mode, delete control and reorder handle, and rows report a selection instead of following an href. Swipe to delete also works outside edit mode, as everywhere in iOS. The web's FavoriteToggle (the star button that pins a page) is not a separate type: use Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton()) and a star symbol, shown in the examples. Edit mode is set with .environment(\.editMode, …) on this section only, which exists on iOS alone; on the macOS host build the section has no edit mode. Android has the same parameters.
accessibility: The heading (star and title) is one element with the header trait; the star is decorative.
Rows are buttons named by the destination; the current one has the selected trait and is also set in a semibold weight, so it is not shown by colour alone.
The Edit button is named Edit favorites and reads Done while editing.
In edit mode each row has Move up and Move down accessibility actions (when onReorder is given), and the system delete control.
After a removal, "Roadmap removed from favorites." is announced.
Rows are at least 44 points tall and the names wrap and scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: With neither onRemove nor onReorder there is no Edit button and no swipe to delete.
Removing the last item ends edit mode; with no emptyMessage the section then disappears.
Long names wrap; the heading's Edit button stays at the trailing edge.
Edit mode controls are drawn by the system List, so they need a device or simulator to see; outside a List the section is a plain stack.
